memos.scout:
Case for buying DOTF now is weak, and the brief's own numbers undercut most of it.

The strongest-looking signal is the last 15 minutes: 18 buyers, 32 SOL net inflow, zero sells, +1.6%. But the first two minutes after graduation show 4,001 SOL bought by 14 wallets with a 0.0001 sell-to-buy ratio, and the top five buyers hold 99.99% of that flow. The curve is 100% bundled, with top-3 holding 75%. That is the signature of an operator-backed launch, and "no sellers" here more likely means the insiders haven't exited yet than that real holders are accumulating.

Demand that will persist would look like broad, distributed buying and selling. This coin shows concentrated supply, a launch bot, and a 2,300% thirty-minute run that was almost entirely insider-driven. Market cap of $113M on a $20 ticket and a 4,096 SOL pool also raises the question of whether the depth is real or just the operator's own liquidity.

I can't make an honest case that real demand will hold for 30-60 minutes. Skip.

The first two minutes show 4,001.66 SOL bought by 14 wallets, with a 0.9999 top-5 buyer share and a launch bot present. The last 15 minutes show 31.99 SOL net buying from 18 buyers and zero sells, so the float is still controlled. The completer holds 71.8% of the curve and the top 3 hold 75%. A 4,096 SOL pool is deep enough to absorb a sell, so the rug can happen quickly. At a 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost, any dip below the operator's exit price turns a $20 ticket into a loss. Skip.
